audit.why: The full layer's stage ownership (Fiora level 1, skill at 2, Jayce 3 through 5, Fiora at 6, Jayce at both item stages) is consistent with the packet chart and with a 48.91% matchup. Level 1 going to Fiora is correct rather than a contradiction here — Lunge is not yet levelled but Jayce has only one rank of Shock Blast and no gate, and she wins any contact. No change needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why for level 6 is champion-wide boilerplate ('six abilities against his four') and never names Grand Challenge or what it does.
audit.why: Grand Challenge is 110/90/70s, deals true damage on the vitals, reveals all four at once and heals Fiora AND her nearby allies if she completes them or the target dies. Against a Jayce who buys no defensive stats, the true damage is the reason resistances are not the answer.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten around the 110s figure, the true damage and the team heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is described five times as something that 'parries your hammer combo', but the page never states the half of it that decides the matchup: if Riposte blocks an IMMOBILISING effect, the follow-up stab STUNS instead of slowing.
audit.why: Riot's W text is explicit. Jayce's entire answer to a Fiora who closes is Thundering Blow, and Thundering Blow into an active Riposte does not merely get parried — it converts her counter from a slow into a stun and hands her the all-in. That inverts the instruction the page currently gives, which is to hold hammer E for her engage.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, the Key Ability Interactions entry and dontsFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns told the player to track Riposte with no duration attached, so there was nothing to count.
audit.why: Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16s — by far the longest cooldown in her kit and the only reliable window Jayce gets. Lunge at 13s and 400 range is the second number that decides whether a step-up is safe.
audit.corrected: Both figures written into breakdown.cooldowns and the dos entries.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Itemization entry says anti-heal is needed because 'his healing fights your pattern' — wrong pronoun, and no source given for the healing.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags this pair for both needs-antiheal (Duelist's Dance vitals and Grand Challenge) and onhit-itemization (Lunge applies on-hit effects, so her damage scales with attack speed and armour alone misreads the trade). Both are real in Riot's text and neither is on the page.
audit.corrected: Pronoun fixed across the full layer; the vital heal and the true damage now appear in the phase reason and cooldown entries.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fiora is called 'he'/'his' in fifteen full-layer fields, and dosFull[2] / dontsFull[1] carry descriptions copied from unrelated template lines.
audit.why: Wrong pronouns and mismatched title/description pairs read as unmaintained data.
audit.corrected: Pronouns corrected; both descriptions rewritten with real mechanics.

notes: The Riposte stun-on-immobilise finding is the most consequential thing in this matchup and it reverses advice the page currently gives, so it is worth a second pair of eyes before it ships: the existing text tells the Jayce player to hold Thundering Blow for her engage, which is exactly the input that upgrades her counter. I stated the rule from Riot's own W text and did not speculate about whether Jayce's knockback specifically registers as an immobilise for that check — that qualifier is the one piece I could not confirm, and if displacements do not count then dontsFull[1] as I wrote it is too strong. Everything else here (the 24s timer, the parry-all-damage window, the on-hit application on Lunge) is stated plainly by Riot.
